newsitem.title: USA: Freezing temperatures damage Minnesota row crops.
newsitem.headline: Freezing temperatures damage Minnesota row crops.

text.p: Temperatures dropped into the 30s Farenheit in parts of Minnesota in the week ended Sunday, causing a killing frost in some counties, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said.
"Large portions of (Meeker County) received a very unwelcome killing frost on Friday night, September 13," a county agent said the weekly crop report.

There were reports of frost in McLeod, Sibley and Carver counties as well. "The green soybeans are black and corn was turning white with a silage smell in the air on Sunday evening," the county agent said.
Corn was 71 percent dented, 30 points ahead of the previous week but trailing the average of 76 percent.
Corn was rated two percent very poor, nine percent poor, 36 fair, 44 good and nine excellent.
Soybeans were rated one percent very poor, 10 percent poor, 41 percent fair, 42 good and six excellent.
East-central Minnesota districts recorded a high of 87 degrees F and a low of 29 degrees this week.
Soil moisture was rated 22 percent very short, 29 short, 46 adequate and three percent surplus.
